description: Rwanda is in the partial launch phase of a new, comprehensive digital ID system, with a pre-enrollment drive initiated in August 2025. The existing Irembo platform continues to provide online government services.

description: Mauritius is upgrading its National Identity Card (MNIC) system to a comprehensive digital identity ecosystem in line with the 'Digital Mauritius 2030' strategy. A new version of the physical smart ID card (MNIC 3.0) was unveiled in February 2024. In September 2024, the government launched the 'Mobil ID' and the 'MWA' mobile app, which functions as a digital wallet for documents like identity cards and birth certificates. While the physical card is in use, the full integration of the digital wallet is ongoing, making the system a partial launch toward a comprehensive digital identity.

Madagascar is actively developing a digital identity system, supported by the World Bank's Digital Governance and Identification Management System (PRODIGY) Project. The project aims to strengthen the Identity Management (ID-M) system and improve service delivery in selected sectors. Efforts are being made to expedite the delivery of unique identifiers during household censuses to provide immediate access to state services. The system will eventually integrate biometric registration and facilitate the regularization of individuals without legal identity.

Comoros is working towards a comprehensive digital ID system as part of its efforts to digitize the economy. {Link: According to the African Development Bank Group https://www.afdb.org/en/news-and-events/press-releases/comoros-african-development-bank-grants-over-9-million-euros-digitizing-comorian-economy-74516}, the African Development Bank has granted over 9 million euros to the Comoros for the Project to Support the Digitization of the Comorian Economy. This project aims to improve governance, quality, affordability, and accessibility of public services. It includes plans for a data center, digital administration platforms, e-services development, and a digital public payment system. The country has a low Digital Identity Index score of 26.05/100, indicating room for development.

Mozambique is implementing its digital transformation strategy, supported by the World Bank's Digital Governance and Economy (EDGE) Project. As part of this, the government has launched a nationwide free ID registration campaign to increase civil identification coverage, which is a foundational step toward a digital ID. Significant efforts are underway to digitalize government services through a new Citizen Portal, an e-payment gateway, and digital signatures.

description: Lesotho has a well-established foundational National Identification (NID) system launched in 2013, with near-universal coverage. The country is now actively working on upgrading this system to a full digital ID, with a focus on verifiable credentials and digital certificates.
